summary.short: Approves the Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime (Budapest, 23 November 2001). The Convention requires Parties to criminalise computer-related offences, to create investigative powers over electronic evidence, and to cooperate internationally.
summary.long: Law 1928 of 2018 approves the Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime, adopted in Budapest on 23 November 2001, and reproduces its Spanish text. The Convention requires each Party to make specified conduct criminal under domestic law: illegal access, interception, data and system interference, misuse of devices, computer forgery and computer fraud (Arts. 2-8), child pornography (Art. 9) and intellectual-property infringements committed on a commercial scale through a computer system (Art. 10), with attempt and complicity (Art. 11). Legal persons may be held liable (Art. 12), subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions including custodial penalties (Art. 13). Procedural powers cover expedited preservation of stored data for up to ninety days (Art. 16), production orders to persons and service providers (Art. 18), search and seizure (Art. 19), and real-time collection of traffic and content data (Arts. 20-21), subject to safeguards (Art. 15). Parties must establish jurisdiction (Art. 22) and cooperate on extradition, mutual assistance and spontaneous information (Arts. 23-28). Several reservations are permitted. The fetched text reproduces the Convention, with the law's title and headers; it does not contain separate operative articles of the approving law, and it gives 24 July 2018 as the law's date.

notes: The document reproduces the bill header (Proyecto de Ley 58 de 2017) and the Spanish text of the Convention. It contains no articles of the approving law itself (no approval article, entry-into-force or constitutional review clause), so no legal_basis relation is stated. The official Diario Oficial text was an image converted by the editor. Internal inconsistency: Art. 18(2) refers to 'artículos 14 y 14' (probably 14 and 15 intended). Preamble-only references (e.g., 1981 data protection convention, UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, ILO convention) are not coded as relations. The in-force status comes from registry metadata; the document states no vigencia date.

thresholds.variable_text: menor (minor) for child pornography offences: person under 18 years
thresholds.value_text: toda persona menor de dieciocho años
thresholds.measurement: age of the depicted person; not specified in text
thresholds.consequence: Depicted persons under 18 are minors for the child pornography offences in Art. 9, unless a Party sets a lower age limit under Art. 9(3).
thresholds.conditions: Applies by default; a Party may set a lower age limit, which must be at least 16 years.

evidence.quote: toda persona menor de dieciocho años

thresholds.variable_text: lower age limit that a Party may set for minors in Art. 9, floor of 16 years
thresholds.value_text: que será como mínimo de dieciséis años
thresholds.measurement: age of the depicted person; not specified in text
thresholds.consequence: A Party that sets a lower age limit for minors in Art. 9 may not set it below 16 years.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only where a Party chooses to set a lower age limit under Art. 9(3).

evidence.quote: que será como mínimo de dieciséis años

thresholds.variable_text: maximum term of deprivation of liberty of the offence, for extradition eligibility under the Convention
thresholds.value_text: con una pena privativa de libertad de una duración máxima de como mínimo un año
thresholds.measurement: maximum penalty under the law of both requesting and requested Parties; not specified in text
thresholds.consequence: Offences in Arts. 2 to 11 are extraditable between Parties only if punishable in both Parties' laws with at least this maximum term of deprivation of liberty, or a heavier penalty.
thresholds.conditions: Offence must be punishable under the law of both Parties; applies to offences established under Arts. 2 to 11.

evidence.quote: con una pena privativa de libertad de una duración máxima de como mínimo un año

thresholds.variable_text: number of items (devices, passwords or similar data) possessed, required by a Party for criminal liability under Art. 6(1)(b)
thresholds.value_text: Cualquier Parte podrá exigir en su derecho interno que se posea un número determinado de dichos elementos para que se considere que existe responsabilidad penal.
thresholds.measurement: number of items possessed with intent to commit offences in Arts. 2 to 5; not specified in text
thresholds.consequence: Possession of the specified number of items with intent to commit offences in Arts. 2 to 5 is criminal under a Party's law once the number set in national law is reached.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only where a Party makes use of this option; possession must be with intent to commit offences in Arts. 2 to 5.
thresholds.depends_on: national law of each Party (number set under Art. 6(1)(b))

evidence.quote: Cualquier Parte podrá exigir en su derecho interno que se posea un número determinado de dichos elementos
